note: Wall-clock and machine-dependent: recorded, not asserted. Every round of every figure is kept (roundFields says what each column of a round is); the medians, quartiles and verdicts beside them are computed from the rounds by bench/lib/codec-verdict.cjs, and tests/bench/ts-codec-verdict.test.ts recomputes them. A cell is measured in-process (three stores in one process) and per-process (three fresh processes, one codec each); its verdict is the per-process one.

rules.quartiles: the element at index floor(q * n) of the sorted paired differences

memory.order: native first on even repeats, TypeScript first on odd ones

readsRetaken: The read cells are one full reads run on the commit 3c5fc796 (tree clean; the machine was quiet, the load in every cell of the run under 6; the bench's load gate was off, `TS_ENGINE_ANY_LOAD=1`, so the figures carry their own load), except 4 figures whose A/A control was outside +-2% in that run and was inside it in a re-take of the cell alone (dense andNot inProcess; runs count inProcess; spread8k iterate inProcess; spread8k iterate perProcess); the re-takes were run with a bench-library knob not yet committed (it has no effect unless its environment variable is set). Cells whose control stayed outside the band in the re-take keep the first run's figure and read inconclusive. The write path, memory and start-up are not re-measured: this branch changes no code they run, and they are the parent branch's committed figures.
